architecture: Dual Ensemble Random Forest Regressor (n_estimators=100, random_state=42)

dataset.name: 180-Day Longitudinal Athlete Training & Biometric Dataset
dataset.split_method: Chronological 80/20 holdout split (no future data leakage)

features.prev_fatigue: Lagged acute neuromuscular fatigue score (t-1, scale 0-100)
features.sleep_hours: Duration of nocturnal sleep prior to session (hours)
features.workout_intensity: Cardiovascular relative intensity (fraction of max HR 0.0 - 1.0)
features.daily_load: Integrated training impulse load (Edwards TRIMP proxy)

targets.fatigue_level: Acute neuromuscular fatigue level on subsequent day (0 - 100)
targets.recovery_score: Autonomic & parasympathetic recovery score on subsequent day (0 - 100%)

uncertainty_estimation.method: Empirical Test-Set Residual Standard Error (95% Confidence Interval ~ +/- 1.96 * std)

known_limitations: Calibrated on 180-day longitudinal running & soccer training dataset; requires calibration for cycling or swimming.
Assumes standard circadian rhythm; shift workers or extreme jet lag require sleep adjustment.
Non-linear infection or febrile illness is not modeled by the mechanical fatigue equation.
Predictions represent baseline expected adaptation; individual genetic or psychological stress factors may induce variance.
intended_use: Decision support for coaches and athletes to optimize training microcycles, avoid non-functional overreaching, and plan deload periods.
non_intended_use: Clinical diagnosis, medical evaluation of pathology, or replacing qualified medical personnel.
